subject: Predicting outcomes with lower and upper bounds at 95% credible interval

messages.author: d6a22ac7ce11aa1b
messages.subject: Predicting outcomes with lower and upper bounds at 95% credible interval
parts:
Hi All,

The attached is the negative binomial script. I would like to predict the dependent outcome from the estimated coefficients at 95% bayesian credible interval. 

From the script I used the rbinom function and probabilities (0.025, 0.5 and 0.975) to predict the outcome. The challenge I am facing is I am getting very big results from the upper bound (0.975) whereby its deviation from the mean (0.5) is quite different from the deviation of the lower bound (0.025) to the mean. Is there something wrong with my script or is there a better approach to this objective?

I will appreciate your help. Thanks.

negbin<-"
data{
int<lower=0> N;                           # rows of data
vector[N] intervention;
vector[N] timeindicator;
vector[N] studyperiod;
vector[N] majaadt;
vector[N] minaadt;                    # predictor variable
vector[N] majlane;
vector[N] minlane;
vector[N] medianwidth;
vector[N] speed;
vector[N] landuse;
vector[N] mediantype;
int<lower=0> totalcrashes[N];            # response variable
}

parameters {
real<lower=0> phi;      # negative binomial dispersion parameter
real beta0;             # intercept
real beta1;
real beta2;
real beta3;
real beta5;
real beta6;
real beta7;
real beta8;
real beta9;
real beta10;
real beta11;
real beta12;
}

model {
### priors
phi ~    cauchy(0.001,0.001);
beta0 ~ normal(0.0,1E4);
beta1 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta2 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta3 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta5 ~  normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta6 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta7 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta8 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta9 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta10 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta11 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
beta12 ~ normal(0.0, 1E4);
# data model
totalcrashes~ neg_binomial_2_log(beta0 + beta1*intervention + beta2*timeindicator + beta3*studyperiod + beta5*majaadt + beta6*minaadt + beta7*majlane + beta8*minlane + beta9*speed + beta10*landuse + beta11*medianwidth + beta12*mediantype, phi);
}
"
write(negbin, file="negbin-glm-CA.stan")
CA<-stan_model("negbin-glm-CA.stan")
set.seed(1000)
N<- 552
phi<-   0.6562249   
beta0<- -3.718973 
beta1<-  -0.0691197
beta2<-   -0.0592218
beta3<-   -0.0691197
beta5<-  0.1116451
beta6<-  0.3486364
beta7<-   0.0188575 
beta8<-  0.0934404  
beta9<-   0.7157746  
beta10<- 0.3966873  
beta11<- 0.0046687
beta12<--0.2639508
comparisonafter<-sampling(CA, data=list(N=N, totalcrashes=crashdata_CA$totalcrashes, intervention=crashdata_CA$intervention, timeindicator=crashdata_CA$timeindicator, studyperiod=crashdata_CA$studyperiod, majaadt=crashdata_CA$majaadt, minaadt=crashdata_CA$minaadt, majlane=crashdata_CA$majlane, minlane=crashdata_CA$minlane, speed=crashdata_CA$speed, landuse=crashdata_CA$landuse, medianwidth=crashdata_CA$medianwidth, mediantype=crashdata_CA$mediantype), 
                          pars=c("beta0","beta1", "beta2", "beta3", "beta5", "beta6", "beta7", "beta8", "beta9", "beta10", "beta11", "beta12",  "phi"),
                          iter=5000, warmup=1000, chains=4)
comparisonafter
plot(comparisonafter)
# plot the output
rstan::traceplot(comparisonafter, inc_warmup=FALSE)

### predicting comparison after crashes
ph<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='phi'))
b0<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta0'))
b1<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta1'))
b2<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta2'))
b3<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta3'))
b5<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta5'))
b6<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta6'))
b7<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta7'))
b8<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta8'))
b9<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta9'))
b10<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta10'))
b11<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta11'))
b12<-as.data.frame(rstan::extract(comparisonafter, pars='beta12'))

# lower quartile (2.5%)
phlowerQ<-quantile(ph$phi, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ0<-quantile(b0$beta0, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ1<-quantile(b1$beta1, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ2<-quantile(b2$beta2, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ3<-quantile(b3$beta3, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ5<-quantile(b5beta5, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ6<-quantile(b6$beta6, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ7<-quantile(b7$beta7, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ8<-quantile(b8$beta8, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ9<-quantile(b9$beta9, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ10<-quantile(b10$beta10, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ11<-quantile(b11$beta11, probs = 0.025)
blowerQ12<-quantile(b12$beta12, probs = 0.025)

CA_lowerQ_pred<-rnbinom(552, 
                         size = phlowerQ, 
                         mu=exp(blowerQ0 + blowerQ1*crashdata_CA$intervention + blowerQ2*crashdata_CA$timeindicator + blowerQ3*crashdata_CA$studyperiod + blowerQ5*crashdata_CA$majaadt + blowerQ6*crashdata_CA$minaadt + blowerQ7*crashdata_CA$majlane + blowerQ8*crashdata_CA$minlane + blowerQ9*crashdata_CA$speed + blowerQ10*crashdata_CA$landuse + blowerQ11*crashdata_CA$medianwidth + blowerQ12*crashdata_CA$mediantype))
CA_lowerQ_pred
plot(CA_lowerQ_pred)
summary(CA_lowerQ_pred)
CA_lowerQ_1<-CA_lowerQ_pred[277:368]
CA_lowerQ_2<-CA_lowerQ_pred[369:460]
CA_lowerQ_3<-CA_lowerQ_pred[461:552]
CA_lowerQ_site<-(CA_lowerQ_1+CA_lowerQ_2+CA_lowerQ_3)/3
CA_lowerQ_site
plot(CA_lowerQ_site)

# middle quartile (50%)
phmean<-quantile(ph$phi, probs = 0.5)
bmean0<-quantile(b0$beta0, probs = 0.5)
bmean1<-quantile(b1$beta1, probs = 0.5)
bmean2<-quantile(b2$beta2, probs = 0.5)
bmean3<-quantile(b3$beta3, probs = 0.5)
bmean5<-quantile(b5beta5, probs = 0.5)
bmean6<-quantile(b6$beta6, probs = 0.5)
bmean7<-quantile(b7$beta7, probs = 0.5)
bmean8<-quantile(b8$beta8, probs = 0.5)
bmean9<-quantile(b9$beta9, probs = 0.5)
bmean10<-quantile(b10$beta10, probs = 0.5)
bmean11<-quantile(b11$beta11, probs = 0.5)
bmean12<-quantile(b12$beta12, probs = 0.5)

CA_mean_pred<-rnbinom(552, 
                         size = phmean, 
                         mu=exp(bmean0 + bmean1*crashdata_CA$intervention + bmean2*crashdata_CA$timeindicator + bmean3*crashdata_CA$studyperiod + bmean5*crashdata_CA$majaadt + bmean6*crashdata_CA$minaadt + bmean7*crashdata_CA$majlane + bmean8*crashdata_CA$minlane + bmean9*crashdata_CA$speed + bmean10*crashdata_CA$landuse + bmean11*crashdata_CA$medianwidth + bmean12*crashdata_CA$mediantype))
CA_mean_pred
plot(CA_mean_pred)
summary(CA_mean_pred)
CA_mean_1<-CA_mean_pred[277:368]
CA_mean_2<-CA_mean_pred[369:460]
CA_mean_3<-CA_mean_pred[461:552]
CA_mean_site<-(CA_mean_1+CA_mean_2+CA_mean_3)/3
CA_mean_site
plot(CA_mean_site)

# upper quartile (97.5%)
phupperQ<-quantile(ph$phi, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ0<-quantile(b0$beta0, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ1<-quantile(b1$beta1, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ2<-quantile(b2$beta2, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ3<-quantile(b3$beta3, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ5<-quantile(b5$beta5, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ6<-quantile(b6$beta6, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ7<-quantile(b7$beta7, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ8<-quantile(b8$beta8, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ9<-quantile(b9$beta9, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ10<-quantile(b10$beta10, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ11<-quantile(b11$beta11, probs = 0.975)
bupperQ12<-quantile(b12$beta12, probs = 0.975)

CA_upperQ_pred<-rnbinom(552, 
                        size = phupperQ, 
                        mu=exp(bupperQ0 + bupperQ1*crashdata_CA$intervention + bupperQ2*crashdata_CA$timeindicator + bupperQ3*crashdata_CA$studyperiod + bupperQ5*crashdata_CA$majaadt + bupperQ6*crashdata_CA$minaadt + blowerQ7*crashdata_CA$majlane + bupperQ8*crashdata_CA$minlane + bupperQ9*crashdata_CA$speed + bupperQ10*crashdata_CA$landuse + bupperQ11*crashdata_CA$medianwidth + bupperQ12*crashdata_CA$mediantype))
CA_upperQ_pred
plot(CA_upperQ_pred)
summary(CA_lowerQ_pred)
CA_upperQ_1<-CA_upperQ_pred[277:368]

messages.author: fc5d3270037d7478
messages.subject: Predicting outcomes with lower and upper bounds at 95% credible interval
parts:
Have you tried comparing to what you get if you do something similar in rstanarm? If the predictions from rstanarm shown similar issues then it's probably not your code and maybe something about the data and/or priors. If the rstanarm predictions look good then that's probably a sign there's a bug in your script somewhere, but I haven't checked every line thoroughly enough to know for sure just from looking at it.

In general (not necessarily the issue here), it can be hard to get the generated quantities block to be numerically stable for negative binomial models. We do all sorts of tricks in the rstanarm Stan programs to try to get around that.

Jonah

messages.author: 8aa9b8cc06fdc99c
messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predicting outcomes with lower and upper bounds at 95% credible interval
parts:
The cauchy(0.001, 0.001) is suspicious as I said before. You
want to try to keep all your variables around unit scale (zero mean,
unit variance) to the extent possible for good sampling.

If this isn't just to hack something to be near 0.001, what you want
to do is set

phi_raw ~ cauchy(0, 1);

phi = phi_raw * 0.001 + 0.001;

Given that this is controlling your dispersion parameter, it seems
like you're likely to get answers very close to poisson.

- Bob

Hi All,

Thank you for the positive response towards the problem I posted. They are helping me a great deal.

Thank you Bob for the explanation concerning the priors,  I have been struggling in understanding the scale parameter for rstan and confusing it with that of WinBUGS, where they use tau=1/standard deviation.

What I found out currently is that rstan use the scale parameter as the standard deviation (which is the reciprocal of tau). Please correct me if I am wrong about this clarification.

Thanks.

The attached is the negative binomial script. I would like to predict the dependent outcome from the estimated coefficients at 95% bayesian credible interval. 

From the script I used the rbinom function and probabilities (0.025, 0.5 and 0.975) to predict the outcome. The challenge I am facing is I am getting very big results from the upper bound (0.975) whereby its deviation from the mean (0.5) is quite different from the deviation of the lower bound (0.025) to the mean. Is there something wrong with my script or is there a better approach to this objective?

I will appreciate your help. Thanks.

negbin<-"
data{
int<lower=0> N;                           # rows of data

messages.subject: Re: [stan-users] Predicting outcomes with lower and upper bounds at 95% credible interval
parts:
BUGS and JAGS use 1 / scale^2 (aka precision) for the normal parameter.
It's convenient because gamma's the conjugate prior and many operations
are easier over precision or variance than scale.

R and Stan both use scale as the normal parameter. The scale determines
the standard deviation of a normal. We like this parameterization better
because it's on the same scale as the location (which determines the mean)
and the random variates.

- Bob
